description: God tells them to stop, look around, and ask for the old godly way. Then they answer Him. No, that's not the road we want.
excerpt: He does not say sprint through the intersection and figure it out later. He says stop. Look around. Ask. Most of the wrong turns I have taken, I took at full speed.
verse: This is what the Lord says: "Stop at the crossroads and look around. Ask for the old, godly way, and walk in it. Travel its path, and you will find rest for your souls." But you reply, "No, that's not the road we want!"
body_html:
There is a whole decision-making process in this one verse.

Stop. Look around. Ask. Walk in it.

He does not say sprint through the intersection and figure it out later. He says stop. Most of the wrong turns I have taken, I took at full speed. I already knew where I wanted to end up, so I did not really need directions. I needed permission.

Then look around. Notice where you actually are, not where you assumed you were. That part takes honesty.

Then ask. Which means admitting out loud that you do not know. For some of us that is the hardest word in the verse.

And then walk in it. Not think about it. Not admire it from the crossroads. Walk.

What gets me is what He promises at the end of that. Rest for your souls. Not success. Not a faster route. Rest. The kind of settled you feel when you are not second-guessing yourself at two in the morning.

And then look at how they answer Him.

No, that's not the road we want.

They asked. He answered. And they did not like the answer, so they kept going.

I have done that. I have prayed about something I had already decided on, and what I was really doing was shopping for agreement. When the answer came back different, I called it unclear and went the way I was going anyway.

The old godly way is usually slower. It is usually less impressive to describe. It often costs you something in the short term that you would rather not pay. And it is the only road in this verse with rest at the end of it.

Notice He does not force them onto it. He tells them where it is, He tells them what it leads to, and then He lets them answer. That is a sobering kind of respect.

Most of us are standing at some crossroads right now. A decision about work. A conversation we keep putting off. A relationship we know needs to change.

The question is not really whether God will show you the way. He says right here that He will, if you stop long enough to ask.

The question is what you will say when He does.

What is the crossroads you are standing at, and are you actually asking, or have you already picked the road?
question: What is the crossroads you are standing at, and are you actually asking, or have you already picked the road?
